findings.label: Conjunctival hyperemia
findings.evidence: There was also moderate hyperemia in the conjunctiva

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Slit lamp photograph of a real patient's right eye in an article titled for HLA-B27 associated acute anterior uveitis; caption explicitly describes very severe anterior chamber flare with barely visible pupil/iris and conjunctival hyperemia, matching the target disease's acute presentation. B: Slit lamp optical-section image of the same patient's anterior chamber showing severe flare/haze; caption describes severe haziness preventing counting of inflammatory cells in HLA-B27 associated acute anterior uveitis. C: Anterior segment OCT of the same patient showing severe flare-related haziness in the anterior chamber; directly captioned as the manifestation of the HLA-B27 associated acute anterior uveitis flare.
panels.attribution_text: Kim and Park. A case of severe flare reaction observed in HLA B27 associated acute anterior uveitis.. BMC ophthalmology 2020. doi:10.1186/s12886-020-01472-3. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: a Very severe flare (milky appearance) in the anterior chamber of the right eye was observed with slit lamp biomicroscopy. And pupil margin and iris details were barely observable. There was also moderate hyperemia in the conjunctiva. b Inflammatory cells in the anterior chamber were hardly countable because of severe haziness. c Severe haziness in the anterior chamber because of flare was observed in optical coherence tomography. Inflammatory cells were masked by the severe flare

Posterior synechia was present in 35 eyes (85.4%) at presentation and developed during follow-up in 6 eyes (14.6%). panels.rationale: The slit beam photograph shows a clear 2+ perilimbal injection, 1-1.5 mm inferior hypopyon, and 2+ cells, which are all standard and textbook signs of acute anterior uveitis associated with HLA-B27, consistent with the case report diagnosis.
panels.attribution_text: Khan et al. Acute Anterior Uveitis with HLA-B27 Positivity after Corneal Cross-Linking with Previous Intrastromal Corneal Ring Segment.. Case reports in ophthalmological medicine 2022. doi:10.1155/2022/2014549. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Slit beam photograph of the left eye. This photograph demonstrates 2+ perilimbal injection and 1-1.5 mm inferior hypopyon observed at the time of initial presentation. There is no overlying epithelial defect or appreciable infiltrate in the cornea. Both intrastromal corneal ring segments are in place.
in_text_mentions: n, CDVA was 20/1000 OS. Pupils were equally reactive in both eyes with no relative afferent pupillary defect. Intraocular pressure measured 6 mmHg and ultrasound pachymetry measured 401 μm OS. Slit-lamp exam of the left eye revealed 2+ perilimbal injection and a well-placed ICRS without extrusion or epithelial defect. Notably, there was no corneal infiltrate appreciated on exam. Anterior chamber exam was notable for 2+ cells and a 1-1.5 mm inferior hypopyon (Figure 1). Anterior segment exam of the right eye and dilated fundus exam of both eyes were without evidence of intraocular inflammation.
